title: Auth forgot password
summary: Single-field 'forgot password' page composing the auth-forgot-password block. Dispatches a reset link via adapter.requestPasswordReset and swaps to a 'check your inbox' state on success.
brief: Ship a forgot-password page that takes an email, calls my auth library's password-reset endpoint, and shows a 'check your inbox' confirmation when it succeeds.

steps.reason: The page-level block — manages form-vs-confirmation state, validation, error display.
Accessible label for the email field

checklist.check: Pass an AuthAdapter via the `adapter` prop with `requestPasswordReset` implemented.
Don't navigate away after success — the block already renders the confirmation state in place. Use `onSuccess` for analytics / toast only.
Implement rate-limiting in the adapter / backend, not the block. Returning `{ ok: false, error: { code: 'rate_limited', message: '…' } }` surfaces a friendly Alert.
[AuthForgotPassword] Avoid: Forgetting to pass the AuthAdapter — the block has no built-in fallback and surfaces an 'unimplemented' error on submit.
[AuthForgotPassword] Avoid: Treating onSuccess as a navigation hook — the block already renders the confirmation state in place; onSuccess is for side effects (analytics, toast). Don't navigate away.

[AuthForgotPassword] Avoid: Skipping client-side email validation in the adapter — the block already runs an EMAIL_REGEX check before calling the adapter, so the adapter only sees plausibly-shaped emails.

[AuthForgotPassword] A11y: Email input has explicit Label htmlFor pairing, autoComplete='email', and required. Submit button uses the canonical loading prop (sets aria-busy + disabled). The post-submit confirmation state uses the Empty primitive's region landmark with aria-labelledby pointing at the title. Errors render in an Alert with role='alert'.
[Input] Avoid: Missing associated Label element for accessibility
[Input] Avoid: Using type='number' without min/max constraints
[Input] Avoid: Not providing placeholder text for context
[Input] A11y: Always pair with a Label using htmlFor/id. Consider aria-describedby for helper text or error messages.
[Label] Avoid: Forgetting to set htmlFor matching the input's id
[Label] Avoid: Using Label for non-form text content
[Label] Avoid: Nesting interactive elements inside Label
[Label] A11y: Clicking the label focuses the associated control. Automatically communicates the label to screen readers. Use htmlFor/id pairing, not nesting.
[Button] Avoid: Nesting interactive elements inside asChild button
[Button] Avoid: Using — breaks middle-click, cmd-click, and right-click → 'open in new tab', and skips the browser history entry
[Button] Avoid: Using <Button variant='destructive'> for recoverable actions like 'Reset filters' — reserve destructive for delete/archive/leave; use 'secondary' or 'ghost' for resets
[Button] Avoid: Using <Button size='icon'> without an aria-label — screen readers have nothing to announce; always pair icon-only buttons with aria-label or visible text
[Button] A11y: Automatically handles focus ring, disabled state, and aria attributes. Icon-only buttons MUST have aria-label. Loading state automatically sets disabled.
[Alert] Avoid: Using destructive for non-error messages
[Alert] Avoid: Missing AlertTitle (reduces scannability)
[Alert] Avoid: Stacking multiple Alerts on the same page instead of grouping
[Alert] A11y: Root renders role='alert' so screen readers announce it. For non-urgent info banners consider role='status' or aria-live='polite' via className overrides.
[Empty] Avoid: Using Empty without an action — leaves the user stuck
[Empty] Avoid: Long descriptions — keep to one sentence; this is a state surface, not documentation
[Empty] Avoid: Forgetting titleAs when the page already has an h2 above (heading hierarchy break)
[Empty] A11y: Wrapped in a region landmark labeled by the title (aria-labelledby + auto-generated id). Icon is decorative (aria-hidden). Pair the action with a Button that has a visible label.
